--- title: "Generative Video World Models" description: "Cosmos 3, Genie 2 and 3, GR-1 and GR-2, 1X, and Odyssey: action-conditioned video prediction used as a neural simulator, the strongest evidence that it works, and the weak-conditioning problem that decides whether it counts as a world model at all." domain: world-models slug: generative-video order: 3 status: published lastReviewed: "2026-08-17" citations: - cosmos-3-2026 - nvidia-cosmos-3-launch-2026 - genie-1-2024 - genie-2-2024 - genie-3-2025 - project-genie-2026 - gr-1-2023 - gr-2-2024 - 1x-world-model-lab-2026 - odyssey-2-2025 - odyssey-starchild-1-2026 - odyssey-agora-1-2026 - interactive-world-simulator-2026 - roboworld-2026 - world-model-survey-2026 - runway-gwm-robotics-eval-2026 - runway-praxis-1-2026 - unisim-2023 - physics-iq-2025 - google-project-genie-2026 - waymo-world-model-2026 - gr-3-2025 - dreamzero-2026 - cosmos-policy-2026 - lingbot-va-2026 - wam-robustness-2026 - fast-wam-2026 - 1x-world-model-2026 - world-in-world-2025 - veo-world-simulator-2025 - dreamdojo-2026 - polaris-2025 - rise-2026 - 1x-world-model-2025 - grail-2026 - openwam-2026 - long-wam-2026 - caster-2026 - dreamcan-2026 - aim-2026 - cosmos-predict2-5-2025 - diamond-world-model-2024 seeAlso: - "world-models/jepa" - "manipulation/vla-models" - "data-hardware/evaluation-crisis" --- import { ActionConditioning } from '@/components/interactive/action-conditioning'; Generative video [world models](/world-models/taxonomy/) are video predictors that generate future pixels from the current frame and an action or text prompt, standing in for the environment to supply training data, policy evaluation, RL post-training and interactive worlds. UniSim trained policies purely inside such a simulator and deployed them zero-shot in the real world . Switch "Video model" from "Listens to the action" to "Ignores the action", and the two futures from one start frame collapse onto the same picture. The action-sensitivity score falls to near zero while the visual-realism score stays put. Video generators show this split: "visual realism does not imply physical understanding" .
## Cosmos 3 replaces a stack of separate models with one omni-model NVIDIA's Cosmos 3 report calls a home robot built from a separate VLM planner, VLA or WAM, and forward-dynamics model "fragmented" and "computationally wasteful" . Cosmos 3, launched at GTC Taipei on 31 May 2026, unifies those capabilities in one omni-model . Its predecessor Predict2.5 had already combined text-, image- and video-conditioned generation in one flow-based model . Its Mixture-of-Transformers backbone routes language and ViT-encoded vision to a causal autoregressive reasoner and VAE-encoded vision, audio and actions to a diffusion generator; diffusion tokens attend to both streams, while reasoner tokens never read diffusion tokens . It supports VLM understanding, video generation and three action modes: forward dynamics (video from clean actions), inverse dynamics (actions from clean video) and policy (both). Specialized results come from separate post-training, such as a DROID policy started from mid-trained Cosmos3-Nano with fresh action modules. Nano has 16B parameters on a dense 8B transformer and Super 64B on a dense 32B one . ## Genie 3 renders worlds at 24 fps that hold for a few minutes The original Genie learned latent actions and generated 2D worlds at about one frame per second . Genie 2 (December 2024) moved to 3D, with consistent worlds for up to a minute and most examples lasting 10 to 20 seconds . In its August 5, 2025 announcement, DeepMind describes Genie 3 as a limited research preview: text-prompted worlds navigable in real time at 24 fps and 720p, largely consistent for a few minutes. A SIMA agent sent navigation actions to Genie 3, and the world model simulated the future without knowing the agent's goal; the test involved no robot manipulation. It lists five limits: a constrained direct action space, multi-agent interaction, geographic accuracy, legible text only when supplied, and a few minutes of continuous interaction . Project Genie, released in January 2026 for AI Ultra subscribers, caps sessions at 60 seconds per world . ## GR-1 and GR-2 built on video pre-training; GR-3 switched to a VLA GR-1 applied large-scale video generative pre-training to multi-task manipulation, predicting future images and actions end to end. On CALVIN it moved success from 88.9% to 94.9%, and in zero-shot unseen scenes from 53.3% to 85.4% . GR-2 pre-trained on 38 million internet clips and over 50 billion tokens, reporting 97.7% average success across more than 100 tasks . GR-3 then switched to a 4B-parameter VLA . ## World-action models now run as closed-loop robot policies A world-action model (WAM) predicts future video and actions together. NVIDIA reports that DreamZero runs a 14B autoregressive video-diffusion model as a 7 Hz closed-loop policy and more than doubles the generalization of state-of-the-art [VLAs](/manipulation/vla-models/) on real robots . Cosmos Policy post-trains Cosmos-Predict2 with no architectural modifications and reaches 98.5% on LIBERO and 67.1% on RoboCasa . LingBot-VA learns frame prediction and policy execution together, feeding real observations back into its rollouts and overlapping prediction with motor execution . Under perturbation, Cosmos-Policy reached 82.2% on LIBERO-Plus and LingBot-VA 74.2% on RoboTwin 2.0-Plus, while VLAs such as π0.5 matched them on some tasks only with extensive, diverse training . Fast-WAM stays competitive without test-time video generation, while removing video co-training costs far more . OpenWAM (October 2026), from Heng Yu, Li Fei-Fei, Jiajun Wu, Ehsan Adeli and colleagues at Stanford, pretrains the Wan2.2-5B video model causally on more than 10,000 hours of robot video. That training raised video-then-action success on LIBERO-Long from 68.4% to 97.8% over the original Wan2.2-5B. Its action expert can generate jointly, video first, action first or decoupled . Long-WAM (October 2026), from Wei Huang, Linxi Fan, Song Han, Yukang Chen and colleagues at NVIDIA, MIT and HKU, found that longer visual history pays off when the video model was pretrained autoregressively. On RoboCasa GR-1, extending context from 0 to 19.2 seconds raised success from 63.3% to 78.7%, while a bidirectionally pretrained start showed no net gain. On real robots it stacked moving cups in 95% of trials, a task where π0.5 and Fast-WAM succeeded in none of 20 . DreamCan (October 2026), from Chongkai Gao, Jiajun Wu, Li Fei-Fei and colleagues at Stanford, NUS, Harvard and Northwestern, plans with a few generated subgoal images instead of dense video. Its training subgoals are chosen to balance whether a low-level policy can reach each one against how far each moves the task. With a 0.1-billion-parameter policy that was not pretrained, it reached 91.2% on LIBERO-Long against 82.4% for evenly spaced subgoals. π0.5 and Lingbot-VA, whose scores the authors took from the original papers, reached 92.4% and 98.5% . ## 1X still fails dexterous tasks, while Odyssey streams worlds live 1X reports that its NEO policy builds on a 14B video model, mid-trained on 900 hours of egocentric human video and fine-tuned on 70 hours of robot data, with an inverse-dynamics model (IDM) extracting actions. Over 30 runs per task it scored 0% on drawing a smiley and pouring cereal. The backbone takes 11 seconds per 5 seconds of video, plus 1 second for the IDM . In June 2026, 1X launched a World Model Lab led by Sam Sinha, previously a founding research scientist at Luma AI . Odyssey-2 (October 2025) generates each frame causally from prior frames and user input, streaming a new frame every 50 ms (about 20 fps), steerable by text . ## Weak action conditioning is the field's main bottleneck The 2026 survey lists causal conditioning gaps first among its open challenges and calls weak action conditioning the technical bottleneck. Models trained mostly from observation history and task intent produce futures "semantically plausible or intention-consistent, but not necessarily faithful to the physical consequences of the candidate action" . In closed-loop tests, controllability mattered more than visual quality, and post-training on action-observation data beat upgrading the base generator . DIAMOND trains an agent entirely inside a diffusion world model and studies how retained visual detail affects control on Atari 100k games . Samuel Bateman, Benjamin Eysenbach, Dhruv Shah and colleagues at Princeton and Columbia (October 2026) trace the weakness to the data. They prove that how much a dataset's actions influence its next states caps the action influence any model trained on it can express, so expert demonstrations, whose next states can be predicted without the action, set a low ceiling . In a simulated pixel-based Push-T task, 500 episodes collected by their AIM method and added to 3,000 demonstrations matched a model trained on 300,000 expert episodes on end-effector controllability, an 85-fold cut in data . ## In IWS tests, generated demonstrations rivalled real ones for two policies The Interactive World Simulator is built on an action-conditioned latent dynamics model. It reports more than 10 minutes of stable generated-video interaction at up to 15 FPS on a single RTX 4090, at a default 128×128 resolution; quantitative video comparisons use 192 steps (19.2 seconds) . In 100-episode mixtures, generated-only versus real-only policy data scored 87.9% versus 90.3% for DP and 76.2% versus 73.6% for ACT. With more real data, π0.5 rose from 73.1% to 88.8%. Points used 100 MuJoCo or 10 physical evaluations, and the simulator was trained on interaction data including real play. A four-task test from 20 initial configurations gave positively biased simulator scores except for T pushing . ## Some video simulators rank policies in real-world order, others do not RoboWorld pairs an autoregressive video world model with a GPT-4o scorer that rates task progress from 0 to 5 from fixed external views. In its fourth revision, 4,186 generated 30-second rollouts gave eight policy-level scores matching the 26 February 2026 RoboArena leaderboard at Pearson r = 0.989 and Spearman rho = 0.970 (p < 0.001); the eight aggregates are the correlation points. The paper reports contact-induced object artifacts and VLM scores about one point above human scores over roughly 100 rollouts . DeepMind reports its Veo-based simulator predicted relative policy performance in nominal and out-of-distribution conditions, checked against more than 1,600 real evaluations. Its episodes last 8 seconds, and its authors call contact-rich, small-object interaction an open challenge . PolaRiS found that the open Ctrl-World hallucinated during object interaction in diverse scenes and mis-ranked policies at MMRV 0.22 . In February 2026 Runway reported a similar ranking test for its GWM-Robotics world model. Across eight vision-language-action policies from RoboArena, with 1,450 simulated rollouts scored by human graders, the policies' simulated and real progress scores had a Pearson correlation of 0.95 . Runway says the study tests policy ranking only and does not predict absolute success rates . In September 2026 it announced Praxis-1, a world action model it is testing with partners before an open-weight release . ## Generated experience trains real policies, but contact-rich tasks stay open RISE ran RL inside a compositional world model and gained 35 to 45 absolute points on three real tasks, including dynamic brick sorting . GRAIL used 3D assets and video-model priors to generate over 20,000 humanoid sequences. Visual policies trained only on them reached 84% success on object pick-up and 90% on stair-climbing on a real Unitree G1 . Yinlong Dai, Homanga Bharadhwaj and Dylan P. Losey at Virginia Tech and Johns Hopkins (October 2026) seed CASTER with generated videos of a person doing the task, then optimize a feasible robot motion in a digital twin . Over 12 real tasks on a Franka arm with 21 trials each, it succeeded zero-shot 76.6% of the time, against 42.5% for a twin baseline that tracks each video's object path exactly . The authors trace kettle pouring and bucket covering failures to physics the twin did not model . The survey calls visual plausibility "only a weak proxy for control utility" and says vision and proprioception miss friction, stiffness and contact stability, making tactile integration indispensable. World-model policies also cost far more compute than VLAs in training and inference, and iterative diffusion denoising adds latency . ## Test action response before trusting a video model's rankings Start with paired interventions that change only the action from identical frames, checking direction, contact onset and object identity before image quality, then lengthen the horizon on held-out transitions. Only then rank policies against blinded real trials. By 1X's estimate, with a 15% real gap between two policies, a world model with 70% accuracy picks the better one 90% of the time . The [evaluation guide](/world-models/evaluation/) gives the full protocol; see also [the evaluation crisis](/data-hardware/evaluation-crisis/), [world models versus simulators](/world-models/world-models-vs-simulators/) and the non-generative [JEPA](/world-models/jepa/).

RoboCasa365 reports a separate, larger set . ## A physics engine keeps generated content physically consistent [Generative video](/world-models/generative-video/) learns physics from pixels, and a plausible future can ignore the pending action; the 2026 world-model survey calls visual plausibility a weak proxy for control utility . Generative simulation moves the model off that path: a solver executes the generated task, layout, mesh or reward, so a mug with the wrong friction still cannot fall upward. ManiSkill3 parallelizes physics and rendering together, including heterogeneous environments and point-cloud or voxel observations . ## RoboGen automates task proposal, but humans still inspect the results RoboGen runs a propose-generate-learn cycle: GPT-4 proposes tasks from a robot type and a sampled object, generates scene configurations, decomposes each task into sub-tasks, picks a learning method and supplies rewards or target-shape supervision . Locomotion, presented as an RL task, uses cross-entropy-method planning with the ground-truth simulator. Manipulation uses SAC with motion-planned primitives. Prompt design, in-context examples and human inspection of scenes, rewards, and learned skills remain. The authors name large-scale skill verification and sim-to-real transfer as open . GenSim used GPT-4 to expand a benchmark tenfold to over 100 tasks, and pretrained policies beat baselines by 25% on unseen real long-horizon tasks . RoboTwin 2.0 repairs generated task code with simulation in the loop; a VLA trained on its data plus 10 real demonstrations improved 367% over the 10-demo baseline . ## Holodeck builds rooms from prompts but does not test manipulation Holodeck (CVPR 2024) uses GPT-4 to build AI2-THOR environments from text prompts. It selects Objaverse objects and proposes soft relational constraints, and a depth-first-search solver enforces collision and room boundaries while satisfying as many soft constraints as possible . Holodeck's evaluation, a navigation model pretrained on ProcTHOR-10K, fine-tuned in generated scenes and tested in artist-designed NoveltyTHOR rooms, does not test physically valid manipulation. The authors report trouble with complex layouts and with assets missing from Objaverse . ProcTHOR procedurally generates interactive houses for navigation, rearrangement and arm manipulation . Objaverse supplies 800K+ models without physical properties . SceneSmith (ICML 2026) adds text-to-3D assets, articulated retrieval and physical-property estimation, with 3 to 6 times more objects than prior methods, under 2% collisions and 96% of objects stable . ## More generated demonstrations raised RoboCasa success from 26.3% to 47.6% RoboCasa's 120 kitchen scenes combine 10 floor plans with 12 styles from architectural references. It holds 2,509 objects and 153 categories, plus 100 tasks: 25 atomic tasks and 75 composite tasks; GPT-4 and Gemini 1.5 drafted the composite blueprints, with human filtering, editing and code. Objects come from Objaverse and Luma.ai text-to-3D, textures from MidJourney, and MimicGen adapts human demonstrations and keeps successful trajectories . MimicGen itself turned about 200 human demonstrations into over 50K across 18 tasks . The scaling study trains a language-conditioned BC-Transformer for a Franka Panda on an Omron mobile base on 24 atomic tasks, excluding navigation, with 100, 300, or 3,000 generated demonstrations per task using Objaverse objects and AI-generated textures. Tested with curated textures, unseen objects and 50 trials per task in five kitchens, two in unseen styles, success is 26.3%, 35.0%, and 47.6% respectively. Individual tasks do not improve monotonically . RoboCasa365 extends the platform to 365 tasks in 2,500 kitchens, with 600+ hours of human and 1,600+ hours of synthetic demonstrations for multi-task, foundation-model and lifelong-learning benchmarks . ## Generators expand a few demonstrations or one image into training data Isaac Lab Mimic splits human demonstrations into object-centric subtasks, transforms them and recombines them for new poses, from as little as one demonstration, across parallel environments. Results depend on SkillGen's trial counts, environment counts and planner settings, trading speed against success and motion quality . SkillGen turned 60 human demonstrations into over 24K, and its agents were 24% more successful on average . NVIDIA generated 780,000 simulated trajectories for GR00T N1, equal to 6,500 hours of human demonstration, in 11 hours . GRS starts from one real RGB-D image. SAM2 segments it, depth and a calibrated robot-frame transform give bounding boxes, and a vision-language model matches objects to supplied simulation-ready assets. A router revises generated task code and tests until an oracle policy completes the task. Experiments cap repair attempts, exclude runtime-error cases from the reported reward average and document failures that bypass intended behavior, and sim-to-real transfer is future work . ## Generative simulation borrows its physics from the engine The push figure separates three layers. Appearance renders the mug, as a reconstruction, texture or video frame might; a physics proxy adds collision geometry, mass and friction; and the simulator integrates the push, sliding the mug by $d = v^2/(2\mu g)$ every time. Cosmos-Transfer1 generates the first layer from segmentation, depth and edge inputs , and in the [taxonomy's](/world-models/taxonomy/) verdict on Gaussian Splatting twins, a real-time radiance-field renderer supplies only layer one . Generative video tries to learn layer three, and generative simulation borrows layers two and three from an engine. RoboRender likewise changes simulated video appearance while preserving geometry, robot motion and action labels . ## Generated content still needs physical and human checks 1. Scenes are only as physically correct as their asset parameters: a text-to-3D mug's mass, friction and center of mass are estimates, and generated assets "often overlook rich and important physical properties" . Calibration is partly automated: Scalable Real2Sim identifies collision geometry and inertial parameters from joint-torque sensors and a camera , and DrEureka constructs domain-randomization distributions . Articulate-Anything raised articulation success to 75%, from 8.7% to 12.2% for prior work . The 3D-generation survey still names "the gap between geometric quality and physical validity" a main bottleneck . 2. Task fitness may miss human intent. Eureka notes that its task metric may not match the behavior a person wants, and its authors call a generated PushBlock reward "amenable to post-hoc human inspection and editing" without requiring such inspection or comparing reward hacking . Text2Reward's generated rewards matched or beat expert rewards on 13 of 17 manipulation tasks . See [reward design](/rl-sim2real/reward-design-mpc/). 3. Scene diversity has specific design sources. Holodeck's authors document cultural biases from the LLM and asset retrieval, with only qualitative evidence that new prompts help . RoboCasa's authors drew floor plans and styles from home-design and architecture magazines . ## Policies trained on generated variations now transfer to real robots Learned world models hold narrow roles in [evaluation](/world-models/evaluation/) and data generation ([generative video](/world-models/generative-video/)), while generative models author tasks, scenes, assets and supervision for physics engines . Policies trained on digital cousins reached 90% zero-shot sim-to-real success against 25% for exact digital twins . In 2026, SimFoundry's object, scene and task cousins raised zero-shot real success by 17%, 21% and 40% . Liqian Ma, Danfei Xu and colleagues at Georgia Tech (October 2026) train a rater network by meta-gradients to learn which simulator settings produce useful co-training data for a real task . With 10 real demonstrations per task and Diffusion Policy on a Franka Panda, MetaGenSim data gave 58 full-task successes in 80 real trials over four tasks, against 23 for uniformly sampled simulation data and 26 for real data alone . Data from settings an expert aligned by hand gave 57 . ## Generators propose content and the engine integrates contact A generator proposes layouts, tasks, textures and initial states; an asset pipeline checks for interpenetrating parts and attaches physical properties, as Infinigen-Articulated does for 18 articulated categories . Generated 3D worlds follow the same split: World Labs' Marble exports worlds as Gaussian splats and as meshes, including low-fidelity collider meshes for coarse physics simulation . The engine integrates contacts, a supervisor labels outcomes, and the dataset records which component produced every field. Engines now model more of the contact: Newton 1.0 adds SDF-based collision and hydroelastic contact for tight-tolerance assembly such as connector insertion . Check asset scale and collision geometry before dynamics, static stability before rollouts and contact parameters against real measurements before claiming transfer. Steerable scene generation enforces feasibility "via projection and simulation" and releases over 44 million scenes . Keep failed scenes as adversarial tests; the [simulator comparison](/world-models/world-models-vs-simulators/) gives the selection rule.

--- title: "JEPA and the Non-Generative Counterargument" description: "V-JEPA 2, the LeCun and AMI Labs case against generative pixel prediction, and the counterargument: plan in representation space by minimizing goal-embedding distance, with no pixel decoder anywhere in the loop." domain: world-models slug: jepa order: 4 status: published lastReviewed: "2026-08-17" citations: - vjepa-2024 - vjepa2-2025 - ami-labs-2026 - world-model-survey-2026 - genie-3-2025 - cosmos-3-2026 - odyssey-2-2025 - interactive-world-simulator-2026 - fast-wam-2026 - ad-e2e-jepa-2026 - dino-wm-2024 - jepa-implicit-bias-2024 - muzero-2019 - intuitive-physics-2025 - ijepa-2023 - byol-2020 - meta-vjepa2-blog-2025 - vjepa-2-1-2026 - jepa-wm-2025 - leworldmodel-2026 - ami-labs-launch-2026 - lecun-ami-techcrunch-2025 - dreamdojo-2026 - dreamer4-2025 - lejepa-2025 - lejepa-world-model-2026 - intphys2-2025 - vla-jepa-2026 - jepa-vla-2026 - wam-robustness-2026 - jepa-wam-2026 - tdmpc2-2023 - h-jepa-2026 - skyjepa-2026 - levjepa-2026 - jepa-unstable-modes-2026 - lehami-2026 - jepa-value-planning-2026 seeAlso: - "adjacent/drones" - "manipulation/vla-models" - "classical/perception" --- import { JepaPlanning } from '@/components/interactive/jepa-planning'; The Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture (JEPA) is a [world-model design](/world-models/taxonomy/) that predicts the representation of the future instead of its pixels: an encoder and predictor learn to match the embedding a target encoder gives the true future . It is the main non-generative alternative to generative world models. Drag "Options tried each step" in the figure and the fan of tried moves follows it. "Plan next move" takes one more step. Planning in a frozen feature space works without reconstruction: DINO-WM solved six environments zero-shot without demonstrations, reward models or inverse models .
## Predicting embeddings skips detail that control does not need A generative objective spends capacity on leaf texture and sensor noise that control does not need. In deep linear models, JEPA objectives are "biased to learn high-influence features" . In violation-of-expectation tests, predictors trained in a learned representation space showed object permanence and shape consistency, while pixel-space predictors and multimodal LLMs scored near chance . I-JEPA introduced the architecture as "a non-generative approach" that predicts the representations of target image blocks from a context block . V-JEPA extended it to masked video, with no pixel reconstruction, negative examples, text or pretrained image encoder . ## V-JEPA 2 adds robot control with under 62 hours of robot video V-JEPA 2 first learns action-free representations by masked prediction on over 1 million hours of internet video plus images, with a 1B-parameter ViT-g encoder and a 22M pretraining predictor. A frozen ViT-g384 with a four-layer attentive probe reaches 77.3% top-1 accuracy on Something-Something-v2, using 64 frames, two temporal and three spatial crops and the best of 20 heads . V-JEPA 2-AC then freezes the encoder and trains a roughly 300M-parameter action-conditioned predictor on less than 62 hours of Droid robot video. "Unlabeled" means no reward, task or success labels; actions are changes in end-effector position, orientation and gripper state. It ran zero-shot on Franka Emika Panda arms in two labs absent from Droid, though Droid itself is Franka teleoperation and the authors hand-picked camera positions. Its four tabletop tasks used image goals, with two subgoal images for pick-and-place, at ten trials per setting . ## Latent planning works on tabletop picks, and successors improve it Control is energy minimization in latent space. The Cross-Entropy Method searches 800 candidates over ten iterations at horizon one for actions whose predicted feature map is closest in L1 to the goal's, executes the first action and replans. This goal distance has no demonstrated calibration to a value function, and the pixel decoder trained for visualization plays no part in control . A separate JEPA study trains embedding distances to approximate negative goal-conditioned value, improving planning on simple control tasks . Meta reports a 1.2B-parameter model with 65% to 80% pick-and-place success on new objects in unseen environments, given visual subgoals . V-JEPA 2.1 adds dense predictive losses and reports "a 20-point improvement in real-robot grasping success rate over V-JEPA-2 AC" . A Meta FAIR design study produced a JEPA world model that beats DINO-WM and V-JEPA-2-AC in navigation and manipulation . ## LeCun's AMI Labs raised over a billion dollars for world models LeCun left Meta and co-founded AMI Labs (Advanced Machine Intelligence), which raised \$1.03 billion at a \$3.5 billion pre-money valuation in March 2026 to build world models . LeCun is executive chairman and Alex LeBrun is CEO . LeBrun told TechCrunch that "'world models' will be the next buzzword": "In six months, every company will call itself a world model to raise funding." . ## JEPA has no steerable simulator, and its latents are hard to validate 1. Every currently usable interactive simulator is generative. Genie 3, Cosmos 3, Odyssey-2 and the Interactive World Simulator render pixels a user can inspect and steer . No interactive, action-controllable JEPA environment has shipped. 2. Latent-only objectives are hard to validate: without a decoder, a reader cannot see what the model believes. V-JEPA prevents collapse with an exponential-moving-average target encoder and stop-gradient, a design inherited from BYOL , and its authors state their adaptation of BYOL's justification as a hypothesis . LeJEPA removes those heuristics with "no stop-gradient, no teacher-student" ; LeVJEPA applies its collapse-free objective to video with a single encoder and projector , and Klindt and colleagues prove that it linearly recovers a world's latent variables under stated assumptions . In complex scenes, most models still score at chance on IntPhys 2 while humans are near perfect . ## Robot results do not yet separate the two camps 3. V-JEPA 2-AC's reported robot tests are bounded tabletop skills. Reaching, grasping, reach-with-object and pick-and-place with supplied goals and subgoals do not establish contact-rich assembly, deformable manipulation or whole-body control . SkyJEPA, a June 2026 preprint from Pratyaksh Rao, Yann LeCun, Giuseppe Loianno and colleagues, runs a JEPA-style latent dynamics model with sampling-based optimal control on a quadrotor's embedded hardware. It reports outdoor closed-loop flight with zero-shot sim-to-real transfer . 4. The camps post similar numbers. On LIBERO, latent world-model VLAs (VLA-JEPA 97.2, JEPA-VLA 96.4) sit beside video-based ones (Cosmos Policy and LingBot-VA 98.5, Say-Dream-ACT 98.1) . VLA-JEPA argues that pixel-anchored latent actions learn nuisance motion , and JEPA-VLA that V-JEPA 2 embeddings discard unpredictable factors . On the harder LIBERO-Plus, Cosmos-Policy reaches 82.2% and JEPA-WAM 79.2% without large-scale robot pretraining, or 86.3% as a π0.5 instantiation . 5. Fast-WAM separates video co-training from test-time generation. It keeps a future-video training objective but at inference only encodes the current frame and runs action denoising on a chunk. On LIBERO and RoboTwin 2.0, removing video co-training hurt success more than removing explicit future generation. That leaves a general JEPA advantage unproven. ## An interactive JEPA world or a contact-rich win would settle it Either of two results would break the stalemate: a JEPA environment a user can steer the way Genie 3 is steered today , or a JEPA advantage on contact-rich tasks, where both camps' evidence runs out. Until then the JEPA line has the cheapest demonstrated path from observation to zero-shot planning , and the [generative video](/world-models/generative-video/) line has the only usable simulators. In September 2026, Haoran Zhu, Wancong Zhang, Yann LeCun and Anna Choromanska tested JEPA world models as driving planners with no driving policy trained, using ground-truth future observations as goals. They report that earlier JEPA models were either accurate but slow or fast but too weak to plan. Their AD-E2E-JEPA projector gives a 100-fold inference speedup while keeping planning performance, rolling out 256 candidate trajectories over 8 frames in 0.8 seconds . H-JEPA, from Yann LeCun (AMI Labs and NYU) and colleagues (October 2026), stacks action-conditioned JEPAs that each predict farther ahead and hand subgoals to the level below. On Visual AntMaze a three-level hierarchy raised success from 18% to 73% with less planner compute . Leonardo Toso, Yann LeCun, James Anderson and Oumayma Bounou of Columbia, NYU and AMI Labs showed in October 2026 that next-step prediction with anti-collapse regularization can reach its minimum loss while discarding a system's controllable unstable modes. The learned state is then impossible to stabilize. They add an inverse-dynamics loss that reconstructs actions and prove, for linear systems, that exact reconstruction keeps every state direction reachable within the horizon. Experiments on CartPole, Walker2D and PointMaze from pixels extend the finding to nonlinear tasks . Romina Yalovetzky, Randall Balestriero and Yann LeCun of NYU, Brown University and AMI Labs (October 2026) replace the JEPA predictor with an action-conditioned Hamiltonian flow whose leapfrog step preserves latent volume at every rollout step . On a simulated pendulum seen only in pixels, LeHami has 2.8 times lower angular velocity error than LeWorldModel over the first ten rollout steps . When a torque-driven pendulum must reach a goal angle and velocity, the best LeWorldModel variant still succeeds more often, 0.636 against 0.304 over three model seeds . ## Use JEPA when reconstructing pixels adds no evidence Use a JEPA-style model when the decision depends on task-relevant change and reconstructing pixels adds no evidence, as in goal-conditioned planning. Decoder-free latent planning already scales, with one 317M-parameter TD-MPC2 agent performing 80 tasks . Synthetic video, visual debugging and simulator replacement fit poorly, because the decoder-free state hides what it omitted. --- title: "JEPA and the Non-Generative Counterargument" description: "V-JEPA 2, the LeCun and AMI Labs case against generative pixel prediction, and the counterargument: plan in representation space by minimizing goal-embedding distance, with no pixel decoder anywhere in the loop." domain: world-models slug: jepa order: 4 status: published lastReviewed: "2026-08-17" citations: - vjepa-2024 - vjepa2-2025 - ami-labs-2026 - world-model-survey-2026 - genie-3-2025 - cosmos-3-2026 - odyssey-2-2025 - interactive-world-simulator-2026 - fast-wam-2026 - ad-e2e-jepa-2026 - dino-wm-2024 - jepa-implicit-bias-2024 - muzero-2019 - intuitive-physics-2025 - ijepa-2023 - byol-2020 - meta-vjepa2-blog-2025 - vjepa-2-1-2026 - jepa-wm-2025 - leworldmodel-2026 - ami-labs-launch-2026 - lecun-ami-techcrunch-2025 - dreamdojo-2026 - dreamer4-2025 - lejepa-2025 - lejepa-world-model-2026 - intphys2-2025 - vla-jepa-2026 - jepa-vla-2026 - wam-robustness-2026 - jepa-wam-2026 - tdmpc2-2023 - h-jepa-2026 - skyjepa-2026 - levjepa-2026 - jepa-unstable-modes-2026 - lehami-2026 - jepa-value-planning-2026 seeAlso: - "adjacent/drones" - "manipulation/vla-models" - "classical/perception" --- import { JepaPlanning } from '@/components/interactive/jepa-planning'; The Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture (JEPA) is a [world-model design](/world-models/taxonomy/) that predicts the representation of the future instead of its pixels: an encoder and predictor learn to match the embedding a target encoder gives the true future . It is the main non-generative alternative to generative world models. Drag "Options tried each step" in the figure and the fan of tried moves follows it. "Plan next move" takes one more step. Planning in a frozen feature space works without reconstruction: DINO-WM solved six environments zero-shot without demonstrations, reward models or inverse models .
## Predicting embeddings skips detail that control does not need A generative objective spends capacity on leaf texture and sensor noise that control does not need. In deep linear models, JEPA objectives are "biased to learn high-influence features" . In violation-of-expectation tests, predictors trained in a learned representation space showed object permanence and shape consistency, while pixel-space predictors and multimodal LLMs scored near chance . I-JEPA introduced the architecture as "a non-generative approach" that predicts the representations of target image blocks from a context block . V-JEPA extended it to masked video, with no pixel reconstruction, negative examples, text or pretrained image encoder . ## V-JEPA 2 adds robot control with under 62 hours of robot video V-JEPA 2 first learns action-free representations by masked prediction on over 1 million hours of internet video plus images, with a 1B-parameter ViT-g encoder and a 22M pretraining predictor. A frozen ViT-g384 with a four-layer attentive probe reaches 77.3% top-1 accuracy on Something-Something-v2, using 64 frames, two temporal and three spatial crops and the best of 20 heads . V-JEPA 2-AC then freezes the encoder and trains a roughly 300M-parameter action-conditioned predictor on less than 62 hours of Droid robot video. "Unlabeled" means no reward, task or success labels; actions are changes in end-effector position, orientation and gripper state. It ran zero-shot on Franka Emika Panda arms in two labs absent from Droid, though Droid itself is Franka teleoperation and the authors hand-picked camera positions. Its four tabletop tasks used image goals, with two subgoal images for pick-and-place, at ten trials per setting . ## Latent planning works on tabletop picks, and successors improve it Control is energy minimization in latent space. The Cross-Entropy Method searches 800 candidates over ten iterations at horizon one for actions whose predicted feature map is closest in L1 to the goal's, executes the first action and replans. This goal distance has no demonstrated calibration to a value function, and the pixel decoder trained for visualization plays no part in control . A separate JEPA study trains embedding distances to approximate negative goal-conditioned value, improving planning on simple control tasks . Meta reports a 1.2B-parameter model with 65% to 80% pick-and-place success on new objects in unseen environments, given visual subgoals . V-JEPA 2.1 adds dense predictive losses and reports "a 20-point improvement in real-robot grasping success rate over V-JEPA-2 AC" . A Meta FAIR design study produced a JEPA world model that beats DINO-WM and V-JEPA-2-AC in navigation and manipulation . ## LeCun's AMI Labs raised over a billion dollars for world models LeCun left Meta and co-founded AMI Labs (Advanced Machine Intelligence), which raised \$1.03 billion at a \$3.5 billion pre-money valuation in March 2026 to build world models . LeCun is executive chairman and Alex LeBrun is CEO . LeBrun told TechCrunch that "'world models' will be the next buzzword": "In six months, every company will call itself a world model to raise funding." . ## JEPA has no steerable simulator, and its latents are hard to validate 1. Every currently usable interactive simulator is generative. Genie 3, Cosmos 3, Odyssey-2 and the Interactive World Simulator render pixels a user can inspect and steer . No interactive, action-controllable JEPA environment has shipped. 2. Latent-only objectives are hard to validate: without a decoder, a reader cannot see what the model believes. V-JEPA prevents collapse with an exponential-moving-average target encoder and stop-gradient, a design inherited from BYOL , and its authors state their adaptation of BYOL's justification as a hypothesis . LeJEPA removes those heuristics with "no stop-gradient, no teacher-student" ; LeVJEPA applies its collapse-free objective to video with a single encoder and projector , and Klindt and colleagues prove that it linearly recovers a world's latent variables under stated assumptions . In complex scenes, most models still score at chance on IntPhys 2 while humans are near perfect . ## Robot results do not yet separate the two camps 3. V-JEPA 2-AC's reported robot tests are bounded tabletop skills. Reaching, grasping, reach-with-object and pick-and-place with supplied goals and subgoals do not establish contact-rich assembly, deformable manipulation or whole-body control . SkyJEPA, a June 2026 preprint from Pratyaksh Rao, Yann LeCun, Giuseppe Loianno and colleagues, runs a JEPA-style latent dynamics model with sampling-based optimal control on a quadrotor's embedded hardware. It reports outdoor closed-loop flight with zero-shot sim-to-real transfer . 4. The camps post similar numbers. On LIBERO, latent world-model VLAs (VLA-JEPA 97.2, JEPA-VLA 96.4) sit beside video-based ones (Cosmos Policy and LingBot-VA 98.5, Say-Dream-ACT 98.1) . VLA-JEPA argues that pixel-anchored latent actions learn nuisance motion , and JEPA-VLA that V-JEPA 2 embeddings discard unpredictable factors . On the harder LIBERO-Plus, Cosmos-Policy reaches 82.2% and JEPA-WAM 79.2% without large-scale robot pretraining, or 86.3% as a π0.5 instantiation . 5. Fast-WAM separates video co-training from test-time generation. It keeps a future-video training objective but at inference only encodes the current frame and runs action denoising on a chunk. On LIBERO and RoboTwin 2.0, removing video co-training hurt success more than removing explicit future generation. That leaves a general JEPA advantage unproven. ## An interactive JEPA world or a contact-rich win would settle it Either of two results would break the stalemate: a JEPA environment a user can steer the way Genie 3 is steered today , or a JEPA advantage on contact-rich tasks, where both camps' evidence runs out. Until then the JEPA line has the cheapest demonstrated path from observation to zero-shot planning , and the [generative video](/world-models/generative-video/) line has the only usable simulators. In September 2026, Haoran Zhu, Wancong Zhang, Yann LeCun and Anna Choromanska tested JEPA world models as driving planners with no driving policy trained, using ground-truth future observations as goals. They report that earlier JEPA models were either accurate but slow or fast but too weak to plan. Their AD-E2E-JEPA projector gives a 100-fold inference speedup while keeping planning performance, rolling out 256 candidate trajectories over 8 frames in 0.8 seconds . H-JEPA, from Yann LeCun (AMI Labs and NYU) and colleagues (October 2026), stacks action-conditioned JEPAs that each predict farther ahead and hand subgoals to the level below. On Visual AntMaze a three-level hierarchy raised success from 18% to 73% with less planner compute . Leonardo Toso, Yann LeCun, James Anderson and Oumayma Bounou of Columbia, NYU and AMI Labs showed in October 2026 that next-step prediction with anti-collapse regularization can reach its minimum loss while discarding a system's controllable unstable modes. The learned state is then impossible to stabilize. They add an inverse-dynamics loss that reconstructs actions and prove, for linear systems, that exact reconstruction keeps every state direction reachable within the horizon. Experiments on CartPole, Walker2D and PointMaze from pixels extend the finding to nonlinear tasks . Romina Yalovetzky, Randall Balestriero and Yann LeCun of NYU, Brown University and AMI Labs (October 2026) replace the JEPA predictor with an action-conditioned Hamiltonian flow whose leapfrog step preserves latent volume at every rollout step . On a simulated pendulum seen only in pixels, LeHami has 2.8 times lower angular velocity error than LeWorldModel over the first ten rollout steps . When a torque-driven pendulum must reach a goal angle and velocity, the best LeWorldModel variant still succeeds more often, 0.636 against 0.304 over three model seeds . ## Use JEPA when reconstructing pixels adds no evidence Use a JEPA-style model when the decision depends on task-relevant change and reconstructing pixels adds no evidence, as in goal-conditioned planning. Decoder-free latent planning already scales, with one 317M-parameter TD-MPC2 agent performing 80 tasks . Synthetic video, visual debugging and simulator replacement fit poorly, because the decoder-free state hides what it omitted.
